Being human isn't a crime. ⚖️ Your child made a mistake. He's not on trial.

Jonah is seven. This week he spilled, forgot, broke and messed up, like every seven-year-old. He's wearing an "L" plate: still learning. 🔰

1️⃣ A mistake isn't a crime. A spill needs a towel, not a trial.
2️⃣ Frustration isn't discipline. Sometimes "teaching a lesson" is really just us running on empty. 🪫
3️⃣ Teach, don't shame. Consequences should teach.
4️⃣ Ask first: "Am I correcting him, or am I just overwhelmed?" ⏸️
5️⃣ Don't teach him to hide. Yelling brings hiding.
6️⃣ Let him try again. 🎒
7️⃣ Correct the behavior, not the child.
8️⃣ The real goal isn't a kid who never messes up. It's a kid who can say, "I made a mistake." ❤️

"Whoever conceals his transgressions will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy." Proverbs 28:13

At the cross, we're not on trial anymore. "There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus." Romans 8:1 🙏

Correct the behavior. Protect the relationship. ❤️ And if your child seems "stubborn," it might be worry.
